thread:
maria: Noticing a sharp LCP + interactivity spike on the dashboard canary from ~08:20 UTC. Charts in `metrics-tiles` take ~2-3s to paint on cold load. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
ajay: Yep saw alerts. Telemetry shows a lot more main-thread parse/compile time.
sasha: I grabbed a flame from the canary session — seems bundle parse + chunk eval is spiking. Could be a new splitpoint causing duplication.
ben: Did the last frontend rollout change route-level prefetch priorities? That was tweaked yesterday.
maria: @ben good call — frontend rollout had a config flip: `prefetch.priority = 'aggressive'` for /dashboard to improve nav times. Maybe it's pulling in extra chunks on initial render.
ajay: If prefetch aggressively pulls shared chunks it can cause duped evals on client when chunk ordering changes. We saw similar with embedlib.
sasha: Pasted the quick log snippet from the canary client: ```
[08:21:03] fetched /static/js/chunk-plot-7a2.js (45kb)
[08:21:03] fetched /static/js/shared-viz-2c9.js (210kb)
[08:21:03] eval chunk shared-viz -> main thread 250ms
[08:21:05] render tiles blocked by script parse 1200ms
```
maria: Oof. 1.2s main-thread block per user is bad. Might explain LCP jump. Can we confirm if kvcache misses increased?
ajay: Checking server side metrics now — KV cache hit rate for the heatmap prefix keys dropped from 98% -> 73% around the same time window. Could be eviction churn after routing weight change.
ben: We changed routing weights for canary to steer more requests to eu-west to test dedicated pools. That may have spread hot keys across nodes and thrashed the prefix KV cache.
sasha: Combining that with aggressive prefetch means client requests hit more unique prefixed sessions, missing prefix cache and forcing full init.
maria: Proposed quick mitigation: roll back `prefetch.priority` to previous value for the canary and nudge routing weight back. Rollback now? :warning:
ben: Deploy-bot: triggered rollback of frontend config to `prefetch.priority = 'standard'` for canary (deploy id fb-rc-321) :white_check_mark:
ajay: Telemetry: after 2 minutes post-rollback main-thread parse times trending down. KV hit rate climbing back to ~95%.
sasha: Also submitted a short-term patch to defer heavy viz chunk eval until idle using `requestIdleCallback` fallback — PR up at https://git.internal/r/redwood/frontend/pulls/842.
maria: Nice. For postmortem + next steps: 1) add a canary gate that watches KV hit-rate + LCP before flipping prefetch to aggressive; 2) increase affinity threshold so hot prefixes aren't spread across too many nodes; 3) add an observability panel in Console that correlates routing-weight changes with client LCP.
ben: Agreed. Also add a lightweight local dev tool to simulate prefix eviction so we can reproduce without spinning up heavy canary traffic.
ajay: I'll open a ticket to tune autoscaler cooldown on dedicated pools — aggressive scale events probably exacerbated the eviction.
sasha: One more: add small client-side de-dup check to avoid double-eval of identical shared chunks when chunk manifests are near-simultaneous. Low-risk.
maria: Thanks all. Saved the canary. Follow-ups: @sasha please shepherd the chunk-dedup PR, @ajay please file the routing-weight canary gate, @ben please document the rollback in the rollout playbook.
ben: Will do. :thumbsup:
maria: Closing thread — I'll post a quick blameless note in #postmortems once we verify stable metrics for 30m.
